results.hook: Disney spends about $12B a year making films and shows; a federal credit would pay back part of the US labor in them.

market.question: Will a federal film or TV production tax credit become law before Jan 1, 2027?
market.rules_summary: Yes if a federal law signed (or passed over a veto) before Jan 1, 2027 expressly creates a credit against federal tax for qualified film or TV production; deductions, tariffs, grants and state incentives do not count.

impact.formula: $24B FY2026 content spend x ~50% entertainment = $12B x ~60% produced in-house x ~55% filmed mostly in the US x ~50% US labor = ~$2.0B qualifying labor x 20% base credit = ~$400M a year (Disney books production incentives as a cut in production cost, so it reaches operating income as titles amortize). Low: 40% US share, 40% labor; high: work moved home from the UK plus uplifts toward 30%.
impact.timing: from productions starting after enactment; full run-rate 2-3 years later

market.question: Will Florida Amendment 3, Increased Homestead Exemption; Lower Cap on Increases in Non-Homestead Property Assessments, pass?
market.rules_summary: Yes if Florida Amendment 3 passes. The amendment raises the homestead exemption and cuts the yearly cap on non-homestead (commercial) assessment increases from 10% to 5%, from 2027 tax bills.

impact.formula: Disney Florida non-school property tax ~ $200M a year (CFTOD district ~$105-164M + county non-school ~$50M; estimated) x 1-3 points a year of assessment growth above the new 5% cap, building over ~3 years = ~3-9% = ~$6-18M; central ~$10M a year by 2029. Low 0 if counties raise millage to replace homestead losses.
impact.timing: first on 2027 tax bills; grows each year the cap binds
